historic_warning: A historic sheet under this network is a BACKDROP AND NOT EVIDENCE. Stage 1 is a modern river network and makes no historical claim whatever: nothing drawn on it is dated, and a channel lying over an 1890s sheet is not thereby attested in the 1890s. The backdrops are here to read the ground against, and for the stages that will make dated claims — not to let this one imply a claim it does not make. Re-use terms for these layers are not established and no sheet image may be published until they are.
_no_keys:
TWO KEYED PROVIDERS, AND NEITHER KEY IS EVER COMMITTED. Every entry with `requires_key` carries a literal `{key}` in its URL; the viewer fetches docs/viewer/keys.json at boot and hides every entry whose key is absent, so a deployment without keys offers OpenStreetMap and nothing else rather than eleven entries that can only fail. keys.json is written by the Pages workflow from repository secrets and is gitignored: a key reaches the deployment and never the history, which matters because a key committed to a public repository can be rotated but not withdrawn from every clone of that history.

MAPTILER, for the eight historic layers. The key is restricted by Allowed HTTP Origins to https://docuracy.github.io, which is what makes it safe to serve at all — and also means these layers CANNOT be checked from localhost, where the same key returns 403. That 403 is the restriction working.

CARTO, for the three modern grounds. A DELIBERATE CORRECTION IS RECORDED HERE. These were first added with no key, because basemaps.cartocdn.com answers 200 without one — and a 200 was taken for a usable tile. It is not: the unkeyed tiles come back with API KEY REQUIRED written diagonally across them, which a status code cannot tell you and only looking at the pixels can. CARTO's own terms say the key is 'required for raster to avoid watermarking', free to anyone up to five million tile requests a month, with CARTO and OpenStreetMap credited on every map — which the attribution control does. Checking the response code and not the response was the error; it would have shipped a watermark across the basemap.
_labels: Generated labels show the Library's own tileset identifier verbatim in parentheses. A number in an identifier is not a date and must not be rendered as one: `air-photos-1250` is a scale of 1:1250, whose bucket siblings are 2500 and 10560, and it read as thirteenth-century beside an epoch selector. Only the hand-written labels carry dates, and those are claims someone can be held to.
_removed_nls:
THE S3 LAYERS ARE GONE; THE LIBRARY'S OWN API LAYERS ARE HERE. Those are different things and the distinction is the whole of this note.

REMOVED: 68 layers served directly from mapseries-tilesets.s3.amazonaws.com, including the England-and-Wales six-inch, one-inch and 25-inch. NLS state of the georeferenced layers: 'Re-use of these layers is intended within a desktop or local environment. If you wish you present these layers online in a public website, please use our Historic Maps API layers, or contact us at maps@nls.uk.' This site is public, and the Library's per-layer re-use table does not list those three, so no stated term permits them here. They remain in tools/viewer/, which is the desktop and local environment that sentence describes.

REMOVING THE LAYERS WAS NOT SUFFICIENT, which is the part worth keeping. After every layer had gone from this file, composite.js still held the base URL of the six-inch bucket and counties.json still enumerated the 53 slugs that complete it — a published index to the removed layers, with a working fetcher attached. Each looked harmless alone, which is why the first pass missed it. Both are out of docs/ now. Found by rewt-86 on review, not by the agent that did the removal.

KEPT, AND ADDED TO: the eight `mt_` layers are the sanctioned route — the Library's own Historic Maps API, delivered through MapTiler under an account of this project's own, with the credit MapTiler's licence text requires shown in the attribution control. Four of the eight carry a contract restriction on COMMERCIAL use, stated on their own tileset pages and repeated in their attribution here; this project is non-commercial. Every field of every entry — URL template, zoom range, file extension, licence sentence — was read from that layer's page on cloud.maptiler.com on 2 Sep 2026 and not inferred from its neighbours, because the pages differ: the restriction is on four of the eight and not all, one layer has no file extension at all, and one has no licence block.

THE TRACER DIVERGES FROM THIS DELIBERATELY, and a reader comparing the two should not take it for an oversight in one of them. docs/trace/ carries the full set of S3 layers, first edition included, on Stephen's ruling that the Library's request concerns PUBLIC PRESENTATION and does not reach a tool that presents to nobody without a token. The viewer carries none of them because it presents to anyone; the tracer carries all of them because it does not. Same source, opposite treatment, one distinction — whether there is a gate — and it is a reading of someone else's terms rather than a technical judgement, so it is his to make and is recorded as his.
_not_offered: OS OPEN ZOOMSTACK is the ninth UK tileset on the account and is deliberately absent. It is served as .pbf — raw vector tiles with no style — so it cannot be a raster backdrop like everything else here, and MapTiler ships no style for it on that endpoint. Drawing it would mean writing a full MapLibre style against the Zoomstack schema, for a MODERN basemap, next to OpenStreetMap and three CARTO grounds that already do that job. Left out and recorded rather than dropped silently.
